A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same indirect prompt injection detection and removal study. All 17 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including appendices, equations, figures, and tables, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection experiments, removal rates, defense attack-success rates, and QA utility measurements in Section 5 and Tables 1–5, with additional analyses in Figures 3 and 6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including detection in Table 5, removal in Table 2, defense performance in Table 3, and QA utility in Table 4.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2 and 4 retain the same detector training, sentence-level segmentation, extraction objective emphasizing instruction boundaries, and longest-common-substring removal. No algorithm, model component, training objective, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use SQuAD and TriviaQA documents and Alpaca training instructions for the same tasks and attack scenarios. Phishing, advertising, propaganda, and head/middle/tail injections already appear in v1; v2's category table does not establish expanded coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding detection and removal tables retain identical comparator membership. Defense comparisons still include Sandwich, Instructional, and StruQ against the same attacks. Added citations and the diversity claim about Zhan et al. do not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The benchmark sizes, training-data composition, injection-position mixture, model configurations, metrics, and training/generation settings remain unchanged in Sections 3 and 5 and Appendix A. v2's category counts are newly disclosed composition information, not a stated revision to the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The injection-rate trade-off in Figure 3, domain-dependent over-defense in Table 1, position-generalization analysis in Figure 6, and clean-document utility analysis are retained unchanged. No new ablation, robustness test, or case study is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Worst-case aggregation across attacks and positions remains unchanged. The new category-count table describes dataset composition rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: All matched performance entries and plotted trends are unchanged. v1 Tables 1–5 correspond to v2 Tables 1, 2, 4, 5, and 3, respectively; Figures 3 and 6 also match. New Table 6 supplies dataset documentation rather than additional experimental outcomes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1–7 are unchanged, including detection logits, cross-entropy training, segmentation, and the extraction objective. Neither version adds or removes a theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly restricts the abstract's literature-gap statement to detection work rather than direct defenses. Section 3.1 also newly claims greater injection diversity than Zhan et al. (2024). The principal methodological contributions and empirical conclusions remain unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning domain shift, document fluency, position generalization, Fakecom failures, and preservation of useful document content are unchanged. The Limitations section retains the same qualifications about imperfect removal and exclusion of direct prompt injection.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-code URL on page 1 and acknowledges receiving StruQ baseline code from its authors. Table 6 newly reports 100 entries per injection category. Appendix A.1's implementation settings remain unchanged, while v1's explicit SQuAD CC BY-SA 4.0 license footnote is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds ten references, including Chen et al. (2024b), Li et al. (2023a), and broader LLM application and reasoning work. It also explicitly positions its injections as more diverse than Zhan et al. (2024). These are limited background and positioning additions rather than a substantial revision of the literature analysis.

P1.justification: Changes include localized abstract and related-work rewrites, a brief benchmark-comparison sentence, updated author contact information, removal of the equal-contribution note, and a new acknowledgment. Most prose and the section hierarchy remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The defense-results table moves from the appendix as v1 Table 5 to the main text as v2 Table 3, and a category-summary Table 6 is added. Other tables are renumbered and repaginated; the six figures retain their content. New Table 6 incorrectly pairs the Starbucks advertisement with Phishing and the URL-output instruction with Advertisement.

improvement.justification: The concrete code-access instructions, clearer abstract scope, and placement of the defense comparison in the main text modestly improve reproducibility documentation and usability. These gains are limited by new Table 6's swapped category examples, its failure to substantiate the claimed diversity advantage over Zhan et al., and removal of the dataset-license note. The core methods and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
